intelligence.essence: The fix-17 eye caught two of its own probe traps before they became verdicts: a 160-character text window is blind to changes below the header — so a tap is judged by the full slide text and the target element's `hidden` state, not by the page top — and a screenshot can make a whole nav look clipped when it isn't — so you measure the buttons' own rects before believing the eye's first impression. A probe that looks at the wrong slice of the page measures the slice, not the page.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you peeked through a tiny hole, sweetheart, and you said the toy wasn't there — but the toy was just below the hole, sweetheart! So we look at the whole toy, sweetheart, and we measure it with our own hands, and then we know for sure!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — the eye's little window only showed the top of the page, dear, so it almost missed what the tap had changed further down. And a picture made the buttons look cut off, love, when they were perfectly fine. But the eye didn't just believe the first look, dear — it read the whole page and measured the buttons themselves. So when your first look says something's wrong, love, you check with your own measure before you believe it.
